name: Jikji woodblock edition
summary: A complete woodblock-printed edition of the Korean Buddhist text Jikji, made a year after the metal-type edition and preserving the whole text.
description: Complete text of Jikji in a preserved woodblock edition.
tier_reason: A particular woodblock edition is fine detail; its relation to the metal edition does not establish descent. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

impact.note: One woodblock edition of one text, made by a long-established method, changing nothing and with nothing later resting on it.

date.label: by 1378 (inferred)
date.basis: The 1378 woodblock edition was printed with lay support for propagation; its scoped availability follows from the documented edition and purpose.

events.statement: 1378 edition was printed for Zen teaching; its availability to that community is inferred.
events.population: Goryeo Buddhist monastic students and supporters
events.caveats: No individual recipient or delivery date is established. The inference concerns Buddhist teaching community availability and does not prove sales or number of readers.

evidence.supports: Describes edition printing for transmission of Buddhist teaching; it reports the 1377 copy number as limited and the 1378 woodblock issue as funded by lay donors.

events.caveats: Same text does not prove that the 1377 metal-type edition supplied the blocks or that one process caused the other.

links.statement: How do the metal-type and woodblock Jikji editions relate? They are one year apart with no link.
links.finding: The municipal heritage account names Myodeok in both publishing projects and BnF identifies the dates and shared text. Independent review accepted the named association but withheld the proposed directed observed-combination edge: the two editions are separate outputs, not shown used together or combined. Neither a common-source exemplar nor a direct adaptation is established.
